To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for any fixed configuration of parameters C, and for any m \geq N, there exist a uniformly good sampling scheme with regret R_{N}(C) which is of order O(N^{1/2} log N) when the reward processes have independent increments.
for the multiarmed stochastic bandit problem with fixed number of plays per arm and Markovian rewards, there exist asymptotically optimal allocation schemes.

(i) the optimal sampling scheme is the one which maximizes the entropy of the empirical distribution of the sample; (ii) the optimal sampling rule is a randomized rule which depends on the sample and the current configuration of parameters C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What are the best sampling schemes for a collection of stochastic processes when the parameters governing the distributions of the processes are not known a priori?
the following question: What is the minimum amount of data that must be collected in order to learn the parameters of a set of i.i.d, random processes.
the problem of allocating a fixed number of observations over a number of parallel processes, each of which is a stochastic process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the asymptotic regret of any scheme is bounded below by the sum over all configurations of the product of the number of samples taken from each distribution with the Kullback-Liebler number between the two distributions, and that the lower bound can be achieved.

the lower bound is attained for every C by a scheme that uses the optimal fixed sampling scheme at the beginning, and then switches to the optimal fixed sampling rule for the new problem that is defined by the current configuration.

the lower bound is given by the Kullback Leibler number between the distributions of the rewards at time 0, and the upper bound is given by an explicit formula in terms of the parameters of the Markovian process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained asymptotically efficient allocation schemes for both the non-Markovian and the Markovian reward processes.
we have developed asymptotically efficient allocation schemes for the multiarmed stochastic bandit problem with and without Markovian structure in both the single and multiple play cases.
we have obtained a complete characterization of the regret for the multiarmed problem with multiple plays in both i.i.d and Markovian reward cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lower bound for the learning loss is still given in terms of Kullback Liebeler information between pairs of distributions.
, in the asymptotic regime, the optimal sampling strategy can be obtained by solving an optimization problem involving only the stationary distributions of the Markov chains.
the optimal sampling scheme is a function of the current state of the process.
